text:
maya: quick follow-up on the pagination/retry RFC — we're seeing flaky behavior when combining prefetch windows + transport-level retries. ideas?

sam: can you paste a minimal repro? is this specific to grpc/http or both?

maya: mostly gRPC. short repro: client prefetches next page token, transport retry replays the prefetch call, server returns 409 / "token already consumed" when the real consumer tries to use it. sequence: prefetch -> retry -> token marked consumed -> client uses token -> error.

jon: saw something similar in search. root cause looks like ambiguous ownership of continuation tokens between client prefetch and transport retry layer.

leila: one approach: make prefetch tokens "leasable". client gets a short-lived lease and must ACK consumption. retries operate at lease level, consumption flips lease->consumed. avoids double-consume.

sam: leases are conceptually nice but add cross-lang complexity. simpler option: treat prefetch as non-retriable by default. i.e., transport-layer automatic retries are disabled for prefetch endpoints. users can opt into stronger semantics.

maya: ergonomics across py/ts/go? we want sensible defaults and an opt-in path to stronger guarantees.

jon: pragmatic proposal: default = disable automatic transport retries for prefetch calls. SDKs ship a language-native helper (PrefetchIterator) that runs prefetch in background with safe retry semantics and local dedupe. server advertises a small flag `prefetchable` so SDK knows to use the helper.

leila: we should also version continuation tokens: `token_v1` (single-use), `token_v1_lease` (lease semantics), `token_v2` (resumable / append-only with nonce). SDKs pick best-effort handling per token type.

maya: backoff/jitter: what defaults do we expose in client configs? customers will want control.

sam: propose defaults: exponential backoff with full jitter, max_attempts=3, cap_ms=2000. For truly idempotent page reads allow max_attempts=5. For prefetch calls default max_attempts=0 (no auto retry).

jon: agree. expose `ClientConfig.retry` and `Iterator.retryPolicy` so app teams can override easily. example (TS):

```ts
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  retry: { maxAttempts: 3, baseMs: 100, capMs: 2000, jitter: 'full' }
});
const it = client.listItems({ pageSize: 100 }).withPrefetch({ enabled: true, retry: { maxAttempts: 1 } });
```

leila: ops-bot note: deployed python PrefetchIterator canary yesterday :rocket:. telemetry shows ~0.2% latency bump for hot paths but duplicate-token errors dropped to near zero in the canary cohort.

ops-bot: Canary deployment: prefetched-iterator-python v0.1.3 -> 10% of pods. Metrics: duplicate_token_error_rate -80% (canary vs baseline).

maya: OK next steps: 1) finalize PrefetchIterator API shape for python/ts/go, 2) add `prefetchable` flag to server model descriptor + server-side token lease support, 3) publish retry defaults & examples in SDK docs, 4) include migration guide for customers that relied on transport retries. i'll open language-specific issues.

sam: i'll own TypeScript PR (sdk surface + docs).

jon: i'll take Go impl and run compatibility tests.

leila: i'll coordinate server schema + token versioning changes.

maya: thanks all. i'll draft the RFC follow-up with the decisions above and link the issues. ping me if you want to pair on text. :thumbsup:
